title: Market basics for fund investors: equity, debt instruments and indices
objectives: Name the main money-market and debt instruments and their features.
Explain how indices and credit ratings are used.
body_md:
## Where funds invest

**Equity:** shares bought in the **primary market** (IPO) or **secondary market** (exchanges), settled in the demat form on a **T+1** cycle (verify).

**Money-market instruments** mature in up to one year:

| Instrument | Issuer | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Treasury bills** | Government | 91, 182 or 364 days, issued at a discount, no credit risk |
| **Commercial paper (CP)** | Companies | Unsecured, short term |
| **Certificate of deposit (CD)** | Banks | Short-term deposit certificate |
| **Repo / TREPS** | Collateralised lending | Overnight or short, very low risk |

**Longer-term debt:** government securities (**G-Secs**), state development loans, corporate bonds and NCDs.

## Credit ratings

Agencies rate the issuer's ability to repay: **AAA** is the highest, **D** is default. Lower ratings pay higher yields for higher credit risk.

## Indices

An index tracks a basket: **Nifty 50**, **Sensex 30**, broad and sectoral indices. Most are **free-float market-cap weighted**. Index funds and ETFs copy them; the **TRI** includes dividends and is the fair benchmark.

## Why it matters

The scheme's category, risk and return all follow from what it holds.

> **Exam tip:** T-bills are zero-coupon, sold at a discount; ratings AAA to D.
example: A 91-day T-bill with face value ₹100 issued at ₹98.50 earns ₹1.50 over three months, with no coupon.
say: The fund's holdings decide its risk, so I always check them.
Higher yield usually comes with lower credit quality.
never: AAA means no risk at all.
All debt funds are safe because they hold bonds.

check.why: AAA is the highest; D is default.
